samples.summary: Images inside table cells are excluded from the copy/cut fix, so the stated outcome ("copying a selected image works") remains broken for any image in a table — a common case in Docs. The guard `layout.blockParentMap.get(blockId) === undefined` deliberately leaves cell images on the old, silently-does-nothing path. The rationale (getSelectedBlocks is not cell-aware while deleteSelection is) is sound as a safety measure, but it means the feature is only half-delivered; the cell-aware serialization path (`getSelectedTableCells` in text-editor.ts:1177 already exists for cell ranges) was not extended to cover a single-offset image range inside a cell.

The canonical subsystem design doc for this feature (`docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md`) has a "Keyboard" table enumerating what a selected image responds to (arrows, Delete/Backspace, Esc). This change adds two new bindings on selected images (Mod+C / Mod+X promoting to a one-offset text selection) plus a documented carve-out for table-cell images and a stale-offset drop rule, and the table/doc is not updated. Per CONTRIBUTING the behaviour should be folded into the canonical doc rather than left only in code comments.

Scope creep: the diff bundles an unrelated rendering fix (selection-tint overlap tested in unrounded layout coordinates, new exported `imageIntersectsSelection`, plus a whole new test file `image-selection-tint.test.ts`) into a PR whose stated subject is issue #870 (copying a selected image). The tint artefact for adjacent images has nothing to do with clipboard behaviour and would be better reviewed/reverted independently.

samples.summary: Layer fit: the fix is bound to the keyboard chord (an isMac sniff inside `imageKeyHandler`) rather than to the clipboard path itself. `EditorAPI.copy()`/`cut()` (editor.ts:3356-3366) fire `document.execCommand('copy')`, which raises the `copy` event with no preceding keydown, so image copy works only via the physical shortcut; any programmatic/menu-driven copy still serializes nothing. Making `handleCopy`/`handleCut` (or `EditorAPI.copy`) image-selection aware would cover every entry point once, instead of duplicating platform-modifier detection to intercept one of them.

samples.summary: Reuse: `@wafflebase/core/geometry` already exports `rectsIntersect` (packages/core/src/geometry/index.ts:45) for axis-aligned rectangle overlap, and other packages (slides lasso, debug-report) consume it. The new `imageIntersectsSelection` re-implements the same math locally. The semantics genuinely differ (core counts edge contact as intersecting; this needs strict overlap), so a strict variant added to the shared module — as debug-report already works around at capture.ts:70 — would be the repo-consistent shape rather than a third private copy.

finding.summary: Images inside table cells are excluded from the copy/cut fix, so the stated outcome ("copying a selected image works") remains broken for any image in a table — a common case in Docs. The guard `layout.blockParentMap.get(blockId) === undefined` deliberately leaves cell images on the old, silently-does-nothing path. The rationale (getSelectedBlocks is not cell-aware while deleteSelection is) is sound as a safety measure, but it means the feature is only half-delivered; the cell-aware serialization path (`getSelectedTableCells` in text-editor.ts:1177 already exists for cell ranges) was not extended to cover a single-offset image range inside a cell.

verdict.reason: The quoted guard exists verbatim at editor.ts:2345 inside the image copy/cut branch (2336-2353): only body-block images are promoted to a one-offset text selection; a cell image falls through to `return false`, and handleCopy/handleCut (text-editor.ts:1172-1190, 1192-1222) then bail on `!this.selection.hasSelection()`, so nothing is copied. The stated cause is accurate: getSelectedBlocks (text-editor.ts:3683-3695) resolves the range against `layout.blocks` and returns [] for cell blocks, while the cell-aware getSelectedTableCells path (text-editor.ts:1177, 1203) is only wired for cell ranges, not a single-offset image range inside a cell. The excluded case is a genuinely supported feature — insertImage explicitly works inside cells (editor.ts:3646-3653) and cell image rendering is shipped — so "copying a selected image works" remains broken for table-cell images. The exclusion is deliberate and pinned by a test (image-copy.test.ts:231-253), which documents the gap rather than removing it. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, the guard is the exclusion itself rather than something making the path unreachable, and partial delivery of the stated outcome is squarely the design-fit/spec-conformance lane. I could not locate the originating issue text in the tree to establish that table cells were scoped out, so the uncertainty keeps the finding.
